overall_summary: Extreme cosmic anomalies, bizarre exoplanet weather conditions, and high-stakes space 'what-if' scenarios are the primary growth drivers for FACTVERSE. Traditional cognitive psychology facts and basic animal trivia consistently underperform, indicating the audience craves highly visual, mind-bending cosmic scale concepts over everyday science.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,023 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) represent the channel's top tier of performance.
winning_patterns.action: Develop a recurring series focusing exclusively on the most hostile and physically impossible-sounding environments in the known universe, emphasizing sensory details (smell, touch, rain type).

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' (488 views) and 'What If You Visited the Sunscreen Planet?' (337 views) show strong viewer retention and curiosity.
winning_patterns.action: Frame exoplanet discoveries as hypothetical first-person survival scenarios rather than dry academic facts.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views across multiple uploads) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) failed to gain any traction.
weak_patterns.action: Pause production on self-help and cognitive psychology content unless it can be framed as a dark, high-stakes mystery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repetitive Topic Uploads with Minor Title Variations
weak_patterns.evidence: Uploading 'The Planet Where It Rains Liquid Metal!' (10 views) shortly after similar weather-based planet videos resulted in severe view suppression.
weak_patterns.action: Space out similar concepts by at least 5-7 days to prevent audience fatigue and algorithm cannibalization.

next_video.concept: LTT 9779 b: The Giant Mirror Planet Made of Titanium
next_video.opening_direction: Imagine a planet so shiny it acts like a giant cosmic mirror—but stepping on it would vaporize you instantly.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that its ultra-reflective mirror finish is actually caused by screaming clouds of liquid metal and titanium rain.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful 'extreme exoplanet composition' formula. The concept of a 'giant mirror planet' is highly visual, easy to conceptualize, and sets up an immediate curiosity gap.

experiment: Test a 'Cinematic Space Survival' micro-narrative format: 'Could You Survive 5 Seconds on the Planet of Burning Ice?' to merge the high-performing space niche with immersive, story-first survival elements.
